metrics.label: Posture
metrics.headline: Torso lean averages 8° — in a comfortable range.
metrics.detail: Average lean 8.3°, varying about 20.0° through the stride.
metrics.evidence: Target: slight forward lean (~2–12° from vertical), held steadily. Both very upright and heavily hunched trunks are flags in evidence-based 2D video analysis (Souza 2016), and injured runners showed greater trunk lean at midstance (Bramah 2018, Am J Sports Med).

metrics.label: Foot placement
metrics.headline: We couldn't judge your foot placement from this camera angle.
metrics.detail: This signal needs a side-on clip — try filming from the side with the whole body in frame.

metrics.label: Knee motion
metrics.headline: Knees move through ~78° each stride — a solid range.
metrics.evidence: Target: ~40–110° of knee travel per stride. Limited stance-phase knee flexion reduces shock absorption and is one of the 14 measurements in the evidence-based video analysis framework (Souza 2016).

metrics.label: Symmetry
metrics.headline: Left and right leg movement look closely matched.
metrics.detail: Knee-range difference between sides is about 5%.
metrics.evidence: Target: left/right knee-range difference ≤12%. Between-limb kinematic differences are used clinically as consistency flags; 2D sagittal measures are reliable surrogates for 3D capture (IJSPT 2023).

metrics.label: Cadence
metrics.headline: We couldn't reliably estimate your step rate from this camera angle.
metrics.detail: This signal needs a side-on clip — try filming from the side with the whole body in frame.

metrics.label: Bounce
metrics.headline: We couldn't reliably measure your vertical bounce from this camera angle.
metrics.detail: This signal needs a side-on clip — try filming from the side with the whole body in frame.

metrics.detail: This signal needs a side-on clip — try filming from the side with the whole body in frame.
